{{nihongo|'''Hakusan Shrine'''|白山神社 (春日井市二子町)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Hakusan Shrine'''（はくさんじんじゃ）is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kasugai, Aichi|Q26101|qid=Q26101}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}.

=== Overview ===
Because there are five shrines with the same name in Kasugai City, it is also called '''Ajiyoshi Hakusan Shrine''' from the surrounding place name<ref name="ウォッチング">Hiroshi Ito, ''Historical Watching in Kasugai'', 1996, pp.34-35</ref>. In addition, an open-air market called "5 no Ichi" is held in the precincts on the 5th, 15th, and 25th of every month.

=== Origins ===
In 1659 ({{ill|Manji (era)|Q1145295|qid=Q1145295}} 2), Hakusan Shrine formerly at Hakusan-yabu in Ajiyoshi Village (today Kusunoki-chō 5-chōme, Kita-ku, Nagoya) was relocated to the present site. At that time, {{ill|Mononobe Shrine (disambiguation)|Q11570698|qid=Q11570698}} (a Shikinai small shrine) formerly on the mound of {{ill|Ajiyoshi Futagoyama Kofun|Q11417036|qid=Q11417036}} was merged, and the current shrine was established. The founding dates of both predecessor shrines are unknown. The shrine building stands on the mound of {{ill|Ajiyoshi Hakusan Shrine Kofun|Q11417039|qid=Q11417039}}, and part of the remaining moat is used as a pond.

In the past, mikoshi processions went from the shrine westward to {{ill|Kasugayama|Q11417038|qid=Q11417038|lt=Kasugayama}} (today Kasugayama Park), but because it obstructed traffic on the {{ill|Inagi Kaidō|Q11596828|qid=Q11596828|lt=Kiso Kaidō}}, during the Kan'ei era the destination was changed to a nearby mound ({{ill|Otabisho Kofun|Q11489116|qid=Q11489116}}). In 1918 ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 7), {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|Q11088805|qid=Q11088805|lt=Kasuga Shrine}} formerly at Kasugayama was also merged.

=== Access ===
* {{ill|Meitetsu|Q30850|qid=Q30850|lt=Meitetsu}} {{ill|Meitetsu Komaki Line|Q6788786|qid=Q6788786|lt=Komaki Line}} - about 10 minutes on foot from {{ill|Ajima Station|Q4699746|qid=Q4699746}}.
* {{ill|JR Central Transport Service Company|Q7862679|qid=Q7862679}} {{ill|JR-Central Transport Service Jōhoku Line|Q7862680|qid=Q7862680}} - about 5 minutes on foot from {{ill|Ajiyoshi Station (Jōhoku Line)|Q4699834|qid=Q4699834}}.

※ It is very near the intersection of {{ill|Japan National Route 302|Q11421440|qid=Q11421440}} (Nagoya Ring Route 2) and {{ill|Aichi Prefectural Road Route 102|Q11494363|qid=Q11494363}} ({{ill|Uwakaidō|Q11360097|qid=Q11360097|lt=Kiso Kaidō}}), but access by private car is difficult because there is no parking lot.
